p: an apostle of Jesus Christ by: See the declaration of such salutations in the former epistles.

He begins after this manner with thanksgiving, which nonetheless (otherwise than he was accustomed to) he applies to himself: beginning his epistle with the setting forth of the dignity of his apostleship, forced (as it should seem) by their importunity which took an occasion to despise him, by reason of his miseries. But he answers, that he is not so afflicted but that his comforts do exceed his afflictions, showing the ground of them, even the mercy of God the Father in Jesus Christ.
Blessed be God: To him be praise and glory given.
mercies: Most merciful.
that we may be able to: The Lord comforts us to this end and purpose, that we may so much the more surely comfort others.
sufferings of Christ abound in us: The miseries which we suffer for Christ, or which Christ suffers in us.

And whether we be afflicted: He denies that either his afflictions with which he was often afflicted, or the consolations which he received of God, may justly be despised, seeing that the Corinthians both ought and might take great occasion to be strengthened and encouraged by either of them.

effectual in the enduring of the: Although salvation is given to us freely, yet because there is a way appointed to us by which we must come to it, which is the race of an innocent and upright life which we must run, therefore we are said to work our salvation; Php 2:12. And because it is God alone that of his free good will works all things in us, therefore is he said to work the salvation in us by that very same way by which we must pass to everlasting life, after we have once overcome all incumbrances.

For we would not: He witnesses that he is not ashamed of his afflictions, and further that he desires also to have all men know the greatness of them, and also his delivery from them, although it is not yet perfect.
despaired even of life: I did not know at all what to do, neither did I see by man's help which way to save my life.
ourselves: I was resolved within myself to die.
great a death: From these great dangers.
Ye also helping together by prayer: That he may not seem to boast of himself, he attributes all to God, and in so doing also confesses that he attributes much to the prayers of the faithful.
that for the gift bestowed upon: The end of the afflictions of the saints is the glory of God, and therefore they ought to be precious to us.

For our rejoicing is this: Secondly, he dismisses another slander, that is, that he was a light man, and such a one as was not lightly to be trusted, seeing that he promised to come to them, and did not come. And first he speaks of the singleness of his mind, and sincerity, which they knew both by his voice when he was present, and they ought to acknowledge it also in his letters, being absent: and moreover he protests that he will never be otherwise.
sincerity: With clearness, and holy and true plainness of mind, as God himself can witness.
grace of God: Trusting to that very wisdom which God of his free goodness has given me from heaven.

none other things unto you: He says that he writes plainly and simply: for he that writes in an elaborate way, is rightly said to write otherwise than we read. And this, he says, the Corinthians will truly know and like very well.
end: Perfectly.
rejoicing: Paul's rejoicing in the Lord was that he had won the Corinthians: and they themselves rejoiced that such an apostle was their instructor, and taught them so purely and sincerely.
day of the Lord Jesus: When he will sit as judge.
second benefit: Another benefit.

When I therefore was thus minded: He dismisses their slander and false report by denying it, and first of all in that different ones went about to persuade the Corinthians, that in the preaching of the Gospel, Paul agreed not to himself: for this was the matter and the case.
flesh: As men do who will rashly promise anything, and change their purpose constantly.
yea yea: That I should say and not say a thing?
But as God is: He calls God as witness and as judge of his constancy in preaching and teaching one self same Gospel.
true: True, and of whose faithful witness it would be horribly wicked to doubt.
For the Son of God: He adds also with himself his companions, as witnesses with whom he fully consented in teaching the same thing, that is, the same Christ.
was not yea and nay: Was not different and wavering.
him was yea: That is, in God.
For all the promises of God: Last of all he declares the sum of his doctrine, that is, that all the promises of salvation are sure and ratified in Christ.
him Amen: Christ is set also forth to exhibit and fulfil them most assuredly, and without any doubt.
us: Through our ministry.

Now he which stablisheth us with: He attributes the praise of this constancy only to the grace of God, through the Holy Spirit. In addition he concludes that they cannot doubt of his faith and his fellows, without doing injury to the Spirit of God, seeing that they themselves know all this to be true.
earnest of the Spirit in our: An earnest is whatever is given to confirm a promise.

Moreover I call God for a: Now coming to the matter, he swears that he did not lightly alter his purpose of coming to them, but rather that he did not come to them for this reason, that he, being present, might not be forced to deal more sharply with them than he would like.
soul: Against myself, and to the danger of my own life.
Not for that we have dominion: He removes all suspicion of arrogance, declaring that he speaks not as a lord to them, but as a servant, appointed by God to comfort them.
joy: He sets the joy and peace of conscience, which God is author of, as opposed to tyrannous fear, and in addition shows the result of the Gospel.
